prompt: why do all airports feel the same now. essay pls

So I just got back from two weeks in Lisbon and the thing I can't stop thinking about is how every neighborhood I walked through had the same three businesses: a specialty coffee place, a brunch spot with avocado toast, and a shop selling tinned fish in pretty packaging. My friend says that's just what tourism does and I should get over it. But I'm not sure it's that simple, because some of the locals seemed to like it too? Could you write an essay that actually wrestles with this instead of just complaining about gentrification. I want something more honest than the usual take.
I'd love a short essay arguing that the best way to see a city is to run errands in it. Like actually needing to buy batteries or get a haircut.

Write an essay examining why some cities develop a strong sense of civic identity (Chicago, Marseille, Glasgow) while others of comparable size seem to have almost none. I'm interested in whether geography, industry, sports, or something else does the real work.
Contrarian take I want developed into a blog post: suburbs get unfairly mocked by people who grew up in them and moved away. Defend the cul-de-sac. Not ironically.

My grandmother's village in Calabria had about 2,000 people when she left in 1958. It has 340 now, mostly over 70. Write a personal-essay-style piece about what it means when a place just slowly empties out. You can use my grandmother as a thread but don't make up too many specifics about her.

Is a border something you can feel when you cross it on foot? I walked from Spain into Portugal over a bridge last year and something definitely shifted but I couldn't say what. Write it up as an essay.

I'm a transportation planner. I'm tired of op-eds that treat bike lanes as either salvation or tyranny. Write an op-ed for a general audience about what bike lanes actually do and don't change about a street, with the honest caveat that the evidence on retail impact is messier than either side admits. ~900 words.
Essay: the case for visiting places in their off season.

I'm moving from a small town in Ohio to New York in January for a job and I'm honestly kind of terrified that I'll be lonely. Everyone says big cities are the loneliest places on earth. Is that actually true or just something people say? Could you write an essay on loneliness and city size that I could read on the plane? I don't want a pep talk, I want something that thinks it through.
write something exploring why every city thinks its weather is uniquely unpredictable

What I wish I knew before I spent a year living out of a backpack. I'm 34, did it in 2023, came back with about $4k left and a weird relationship to owning things. Help me write this as a personal essay, first person, honest about the parts that were boring.
Compose an essay on the ethics of 'dark tourism': visiting Chernobyl, Auschwitz, the 9/11 memorial, the killing fields. When is it witness and when is it spectacle?
Why maps that put north at the top are fine actually and the people who post upside-down world maps to blow your mind are missing the point. 1000ish words, op-ed tone.
Why are train stations so much nicer than bus stations? Not just in the US, seemingly everywhere. I want an essay that actually tries to answer it.

ok so this might be dumb but I've noticed that whenever I travel I end up spending way more time looking at the grocery stores than the museums. like I'll skip the Prado but spend 45 minutes in a Mercadona. my partner thinks this is insane. write me an essay defending the supermarket as the real museum of a country? or tell me why I'm wrong, either way

Write an essay on how rivers have shaped which cities became capitals, and whether that logic still matters in an era when Brasília, Canberra and Astana were basically drawn on a blank map. I'd like it to end somewhere a bit surprising.
The underrated pleasure of a layover. 600-800 words, light but not fluffy.

Every travel influencer says 'travel like a local.' I think that's mostly a fantasy and kind of condescending to actual locals. Write an essay that takes this seriously: is it possible, is it even desirable, and what's the more honest alternative?

I teach 8th grade geography and my students genuinely do not believe that where you're born shapes most of your life. Write a short essay (maybe 700 words) I could read aloud to them that makes the case without being preachy or making them feel guilty.
Essay on why mountain people and coastal people seem different.

I've lived in the same apartment in Montreal for eleven years. My neighborhood has changed around me: the hardware store is a wine bar, the Portuguese bakery is still there somehow. I want an essay about staying put while a place changes, from the perspective of someone who didn't leave. Not nostalgic exactly. More like, what do you owe a place and what does it owe you?
Argue that most 'hidden gems' should stay hidden and that travel writers are partly responsible for ruining the places they love.

Why do some old city centers survive as living places (Bologna, Kyoto) while others turn into theme parks (Venice, Dubrovnik)? Is it just numbers of tourists or something about how they're governed? Essay please
the night bus. that's the topic. write something good about it
Why index funds are boring and why that's the point. Short essay.

I'm 41 and I have $11,000 saved for retirement. I see these articles saying I should have 3x my salary by now (I make $68k) and I feel like a failure. I don't want a financial plan, I want an essay about the whole 'you should have X by age Y' genre of advice and whether it helps or hurts people like me. Be honest, don't just tell me it's fine.
Make the case that renting is not 'throwing money away.' Op-ed voice, numbers welcome but don't drown it in a spreadsheet.

What I wish I'd known about money at 22. I'm 58, retired early-ish from nursing, made some good choices and a couple of real dumb ones (a timeshare, a friend's restaurant). Write it as a personal essay in my voice, warm but not saccharine.
Write an essay examining why people who win the lottery so often end up no better off, and what that says about wealth as a skill versus wealth as a quantity.

is it actually rational to keep an emergency fund in a savings account earning 4% when the market averages like 10%? I keep going back and forth. write me something that thinks this through like an essay rather than a listicle

I'd like an essay questioning the FIRE movement. Not dunking on it, I followed it for years. But I've started to think 'retire at 40' is a strange goal for people who mostly like their jobs. Around 1200 words.

I'm a CPA. Every January clients ask me whether they should pay off their 3% mortgage early. Write a blog post that explains why the math and the feeling point in different directions here, and why the feeling isn't necessarily wrong. Audience: smart non-specialists.
Essay on the strange morality of tipping, and why the tip screen at the self-checkout coffee kiosk feels like a small moral crisis.

Why do people feel richer when they pay off a $3,000 credit card than when their 401k goes up $3,000 in a week? Write it up as an essay. I suspect there's something deeper going on than 'mental accounting'.

My dad never trusted banks. Kept cash in a coffee can, literally, and bought gold coins every few years. He died last spring and we found about $40k in various places around the house. Part of me thinks he was paranoid and lost out on decades of compounding. Part of me thinks he knew something about security that I don't, since he grew up in Argentina during the 80s. Can you write an essay about what money means to people who've watched it fail? I'd like it to be fair to him.
why budgeting apps don't work for most people. op-ed, punchy
Write something exploring whether it's possible to talk about money with friends without it getting weird, and what we lose by staying silent about salaries.
I'd love an essay on why the 4% rule became sacred. Where it came from (Bengen, 1994), what assumptions it smuggles in, and whether a 30-year rule makes any sense for someone retiring at 50.

My wife and I combined finances after 6 years of marriage and it was weirdly harder emotionally than the wedding. Write a personal essay on merging money in a relationship, what it reveals, what it costs. Can be from a generic 'we' perspective.
Argue that buying individual stocks is mostly a hobby, and that's fine, as long as people are honest that it's entertainment.
Essay: is frugality a virtue?

I'm a high school senior and I just got my first real paycheck from a summer job ($2,340 after taxes). My uncle told me to put it all in a Roth IRA, my mom says save it for college, and I kind of want to buy a used car. Can you write an essay about how to think about your very first money? Not telling me what to do exactly, more about how to decide.
Why lifestyle inflation is underrated. Hear me out: if you never spend more as you earn more, what was the point?
Write an essay on why so many smart people get pulled into get-rich-quick schemes, crypto, MLMs, options trading, real estate seminars. I don't think it's stupidity. What is it?

An essay on inheritance: should parents leave money to their children at all, or does it do more harm than good? I'd like it to take Warren Buffett's 'enough to do anything but not enough to do nothing' line as a starting point and push against it a little.
Write a short reflective piece on the gap between what my grandparents' house cost in 1972 ($24,500) and what it sold for last month ($690,000), and what that number actually means for my generation.

Everyone says 'time in the market beats timing the market.' I believe it, mostly. But it's also exactly what the people who sell index funds would say. Write an essay that pressure tests that idea honestly. What would have to be true for it to be wrong?
the case against financial advisors who charge 1% AUM. essay, make it sharp but fair

I make $180k and still feel broke. I know how that sounds. I'd like an essay about why high earners in expensive cities so often feel poor, that doesn't just sneer at them and doesn't let them off the hook either.
